analysis: Level discordance, series A versus series B1
specification: The model-to-notification ratio and its Bland–Altman limits were recomputed with series B1 (by date of final review) as the denominator instead of series A (by date of onset)
result: Series A: geometric mean ratio 6.64× (limits of agreement 2.19–20.14×); 2023 ratio 3.69×. Series B1: geometric mean ratio 6.40× (limits of agreement 2.02–20.28×); 2023 ratio 3.55×
conclusion: The gap is not sensitive to the choice of official series: series B1 runs only 3.6–5.1% above series A, whereas the model estimate is 3.7-fold higher. Both series therefore yield the same conclusion.

analysis: Provincial inequality: ÷2 correction versus proportion-normalised allocation
specification: The uncorrected reported values were reconstructed by doubling the corrected provincial counts and provincial counts were then re-derived without assuming any multiplier, as province value = official national total × (reported province / reported national); incidence rates and their annual Gini coefficients were recomputed for 2004–2024
result: Maximum absolute difference in provincial counts = 0.0000 cases over 21 province-years; maximum absolute difference in the annual Gini coefficient of incidence rates = 0.000050 (0.5366 in 2004 to 0.2657 in 2024 under both procedures)
conclusion: Because the duplication applied a single uniform factor to every province, halving the reported value and rescaling to the official national total are algebraically identical. The inequality result therefore does not depend on the multiplier being correct.

specification: Full 1990–2023 series (primary specification) versus the 2004–2023 window matched to the notification series
conclusion: The modelled trajectory is close to flat on either window (−0.24% and −1.01% per year), an order of magnitude smaller than the −10.0% annual decline in notified early syphilis; the contrast is therefore not an artefact of window choice.
